status_at_registration: The 287.1 results are known. This is a post-hoc exploratory correction, never pooled with or presented as confirmatory replication of 287.1.

reason.v1_design_defect: Raw, summary, and native representations exposed event IDs while the answer contract demanded canonical F/D/S/U/N IDs that only deterministic packets exposed. Exact-ID retention therefore measured answer-key availability, not retention.
reason.v1_runtime_availability: Claude returned subscription spend-limit status in a neutral harness probe. Grok succeeded only when pointed at Orchestra's already-managed GROK_HOME; the v1 default home was unauthenticated.
reason.non_rerun_rule: No 287.1 cell is replaced or rerun. Version 2 uses a corrected representation contract, retains all 287.1 data, and is labelled exploratory because the investigator has seen version 1 outcomes.

changes: Each raw event receives explicit state_ids metadata linking observable content to canonical IDs; all mechanisms therefore have access to the same answer vocabulary.
The source-generated summary uses Codex Luna because Claude is unavailable; it is frozen for both available targets.
Available targets are Codex Luna and Grok 4.6. Claude is recorded unavailable, not substituted.
Grok uses the existing managed subscription home at /home/kesha/orchestra/data/grok-home without editing config or credentials.
Grok parser consumes the CLI structuredOutput field; the neutral preflight returned status=ok before registration.
Task contents, distractor count, output schema, scoring rubric, timeout, no-rerun rule, and mechanism definitions remain version 1.

unavailable_targets.claude: subscription spend limit; neutral probe returned api_error_status=429 and zero usage

design.ordering: task, mechanism, target; target order alternates Codex/Grok by task index
design.winner_rule: Same as protocol 287.1; compare only within the 287.2 corpus and label every conclusion exploratory.
